messages:
maria: Quick bring-up note — ran Liminal12B v1 on int8 and int4 profiles this morning. Sharing raw smoke numbers and a proposed GTN recommendation.
leo: Nice. what do the latencies look like?
maria: single-token p95 (chat-like): fp16 ~ 24ms, int8 ~ 28ms, int4 ~ 37ms on p4d. Throughput (concurrent=8): fp16 380 tok/s, int8 470 tok/s, int4 610 tok/s.
owen: int4 throughput looks great, but what's quality? any regressions on our long-form QA slices?
maria: ran 3 eval slices (short answer, summarization, multi-turn QA) — aggregated exact-match/ROUGE drops: int8 ~ -0.8% EM, -0.7 ROUGE; int4 ~ -3.2% EM, -2.9 ROUGE versus fp16 baseline. Failure modes in int4: entity hallucination in multi-turn and occasional truncation on long summaries.
ashley: product POV: acceptable if cost savings are big and we route tricky prompts to higher-fidelity models. numbers?
maria: unit-econ: token cost (infra only) per 1k tokens: fp16 $0.021, int8 $0.015, int4 $0.009. So int4 is ~57% cheaper vs fp16.
leo: that's compelling. Do we have a sanity check on tail latency for int4? p99?
maria: p99 single-token: fp16 62ms, int8 85ms, int4 140ms. p99 grows nonlinearly for int4 under mixed workload because of kernel fallback in long sequences.
owen: so tradeoff map: int4 = big cost savings + higher throughput but worse tail latency + small quality drop. Can we hybrid route?
maria: proposed hybrid routing policy: default route = int8, fallback to fp16 for prompts flagged by our complexity classifier (longer than 512 tokens, high entity density, or conversation depth > 3). Int4 only as burst capacity for low-risk short prompts (one-shot Q/A where recall tolerance is higher).
ashley: for GTN guidance, suggest we offer int8 as recommended config for most customers, advertise int4 as 'cost-savings lab' with clear caveats. Also provide a canned routing recipe for product teams.
leo: do we have numbers for cost impact using our sample traffic mix?
maria: yes — applied to sample_traffic_v2 (mix: 60% short chat, 25% summarization, 15% long QA). Simulated monthly cost delta for 10M tokens: fp16 $210, int8 $150, int4 $90. With hybrid routing (int8 + fp16 for complex) we estimate $130.
owen: quality delta on hybrid?
maria: hybrid keeps aggregated EM drop to ~ -0.6% vs fp16 because complex prompts stay on fp16. Summarization ROUGE loss ~ -0.5.
bench-bot: Auto-report: perf artifacts uploaded -> s3://redwood-inference/bench/liminal12b/3309123456/ (includes detailed per-slice logs and per-kernel timing).
leo: thanks. any operational risks? memory OOMs, slow warmup, cache issues?
maria: noticed cold-start kv-cache penalty for int4 serving until kv warmup completes ~ first 3 tokens are ~3x slower on int4. Also occasional CUDA kernel fallback log lines for sequence > 2048 causing spikes. Ops note: add warmstart priming or short-prefill to mitigate.
owen: actionable recs?
maria: 1) Default model config: int8 with quantized-kv cache enabled; 2) Routing rule: complexity classifier -> fp16; 3) Offer int4 in Dedicated as opt-in burst only; 4) Docs: explicit scorecard + regression notes + sample rollout flag (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%); 5) Alerts: set quality regression threshold at 1% EM drop per slice for rollback.
nashley: GTM blurb draft: "Liminal12B on Redwood: best-in-class throughput for cost-sensitive workloads — recommend int8 for production, int4 for non-critical scaled cost savings. See hybrid routing playbook."
leo: can we capture an A/B plan for product teams?
maria: plan in thread: canary on 5% users with logging of fidelity signals + human review on top-3 failure cases after 24h -> promote if no slice shows >1% degradation.
owen: I'll pick up the canary automation ticket.
nashley: I'll prepare GTN note and sample customer email.
maria: thanks — will push bench artifacts and add a short runbook to the repo. :thumbsup:
bench-bot: CI snapshot: tests passed (smoke & perf), full-eval queued (ETA 6h).
